strategy.summary: Reproduce the StringDType has_nan_na bug by building NumPy from source at the buggy commit 8ac8883df2e7 and running the new nan-like-sentinel tests in numpy/_core/tests/test_stringdtype.py. Those tests assert that float16/32/64, longdouble and complex inputs cast to, and setitem into, the na_object sentinel when it is NaN-like, and that strings cast to float/complex yield NaN. On the buggy revision the sentinel identity checks fail; on the fixed revision they pass. The build is the dominant cost and the main source of uncertainty, since the cast code is C.

pip_packages: hypothesis (optional, not needed for the selected tests)
cython (only as pulled in by the pyproject build-requirements)
system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest numpy/_core/tests/test_stringdtype.py -k 'nan_na or cfloat or nan_is_not_missing or string_na_to_numeric or non_native' -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 8ac8883df2e7 the selected tests (notably test_float_to_string_nan_na_consistent, test_cfloat_to_string_nan_na, test_setitem_cfloat_nan and test_string_na_to_numeric_is_nan) FAIL because the NaN-like sentinel identity assertions do not hold, since has_nan_na is ignored. On the fixed revision (PR #31825 applied) the same selection PASSES. The transition from failing to passing is the criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np; dt=np.dtypes.StringDType(na_object=np.nan); print(np.array([np.nan],dtype='f4').astype(dt)[0] is np.nan)"

input_output_examples.buggy_output: element 1 is the string 'nan' rather than the na_object sentinel (inferred from the ignored flag; not stated as a literal output)
input_output_examples.expected_output: element 0 == '1.5', element 1 is the na_object sentinel, element 2 == '-2.0'

risks: The commit log says ComplexWarning was removed, but the test file imports numpy.exceptions.ComplexWarning and uses pytest.warns(ComplexWarning) in test_roundtrip_float_through_complex_and_string. If the fixed revision no longer exposes that name, the module fails to import on both revisions and the transition is lost. The roundtrip test is not in the selection above for this reason; verify the import at the fixed commit before trusting results.
The test diff does not add an itertools import; the roundtrip test relies on itertools already being imported in the file. Confirm this at the buggy commit, or the module fails to collect.

longdouble behaviour depends on platform. On x86 Linux longdouble is 80-bit extended; on Windows and some ARM builds it equals float64, so longdouble cases may not discriminate there. The reproduction is only confirmed on a platform where longdouble is wider than float64.
The longdouble overflow concern raised by a bot was not confirmed; it is not a planned check, so an unexpected result there is not evidence for or against the transition.

The strided field-view test and the non-native byteorder tests depend on alignment and byte-swap behaviour. They are plausibly platform-sensitive, and a failure there may reflect the environment rather than the bug.

No Python version, compiler version, or meson-python version is documented. The era constraints are all unbounded, and no pins are documented, so the build relies on the pyproject build requirements rather than era-inferred pins. A build failure may therefore be a toolchain-version issue, not the bug.
The bug is observable only in a C-built extension. Editable installs must be rebuilt at each checkout, or the tests will run against stale binaries and report a false pass or fail.

The supplied test_command uses numpy.test(), which runs the whole suite and is not selective. The replacement pytest selection is used instead. Running the whole suite is not needed to observe the transition.
Under a sanitizer build or a 32-bit platform the behaviour may not match; it has not been shown to exist outside a standard 64-bit release build.

oracle.reference_source: the developer test assertions in the PR diff (identity checks against the na_object sentinel and string equality)
oracle.why: Sentinel identity (is) and exact string comparisons decide pass or fail; no numeric tolerance is involved.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 8ac8883df2e7 the float-to-StringDType cast with has_nan_na ignores the NaN-like flag, so the NaN element becomes the string 'nan' rather than the sentinel. The assertion arr[1] is nan_like_na_object then raises AssertionError, so the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With PR #31825 applied, NaN values (and complex values with any NaN component) map to the na_object sentinel, and string-to-float conversion of the sentinel yields NPY_NAN. All identity and equality assertions hold, so the test passes.
